messages:
alice_acme: hey team, ran into something weird during a long demo. our org had ~15k credits left, started a long streaming job, and 2h later the UI showed 0 and API returned 429. then at next midnight it refilled. why did credits drop midstream?

jess_support: ugh, sorry to hear that. can you paste the org id and the rough timestamps?

alice_acme: org: acme-inc-42, started ~1768879200, saw 429 at ~1768882900. no plan change.

jess_support: ok filing for escalation. mike, any known issues with streaming and bucket accounting? :thinking:

mike_backend: short answer: streaming counts tokens as they are accepted by the router; long-lived connections + retries can hammer the monthly bucket if requests are retried or chunked oddly. can you confirm if client retried on partial responses?

alice_acme: client uses a reconnect-on-timeout pattern, and we do chunked messages every 20s. not aggressive but there were a few reconnects around 1768881500 when the demo network flaked.

mike_backend: that aligns. two things to watch: 1) longpoll/stream reconnects can re-send prompts if client doesn't dedupe server-side, 2) edge cache and quota visibility can lag. the API enforces quota at request-processing time (token debit), UI refreshes later.

jess_support: for immediate mitigation, recommend turning on client-side idempotency (generate request_id per logical prompt) and exponential backoff on reconnects. also shorten chunk interval if possible.

alice_acme: thanks. is there a server-side guard we can enable so retries don't double-charge?

mike_backend: we have a request dedupe header we can enable from the edge (X-Request-Id). if present the router will attempt best-effort dedupe for duplicates within ~30s window, but it isn't perfect for multi-chunk flows. longer term, infra will add more robust streaming dedupe.

jess_support: logged internal ticket INF-2026 to investigate stale quota cache during background backfills. note: there was a billing backfill job last week that briefly reprocessed some long-running streams — possible overlap.

infra-bot: Incident created: INF-2026 - billing/backfill causing transient double-draw on streaming requests (https://redwood/infra/INF-2026) :white_check_mark:

mike_backend: root-cause hypothesis: during backfill the token accounting job replayed accepted tokens for a subset of streams that had intermittent reconnections; without dedupe those tokens were applied again. working theory, need audit logs.

jess_support: action items for acme: 1) enable X-Request-Id on client, 2) add exponential backoff and jitter on reconnects, 3) split very large logical prompts to avoid long-lived open streams. we'll also credit your org for the unexpected draw while we investigate.

alice_acme: appreciate it. can you confirm when the credit will be applied? we need it for the demo tomorrow.
jess_support: I'll submit a billing adjustment ticket now and cc finance. expect a provisional credit within 2 business hours, final after audit. :thumbsup:

mike_backend: follow-up: if you can share a minimal repro (client logs + request_id pattern) we can use it to validate the fix and add a regression test. you can drop logs to the support upload link.

alice_acme: will do, uploading in ~30m. thanks everyone.

jess_support: thanks — keeping thread open until INF-2026 has a root cause and we confirm the credit.

alice_acme: noted, thanks again! :pray:
